title: Don't Fear the Model Router
concept: A hand at the harbour fork
medium: Flat cut-paper editorial collage with monochrome photographic hand
thesis: Model routing is a testable choice of the suitable specialist, not proof that downstream work succeeded.

tensions: An elegant final answer can hide the wrong route.
Cheap requests and specialist work should not share the same expensive vessel.
Monitoring valid decisions differs from controlled accuracy tests.
avoid: blue and rust studio catalog imagery

prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create a beautiful sophisticated independent-magazine editorial hero image, a wide landscape 16:9 artwork for an essay about choosing the right specialist AI model for a task and checking the choice. The visual metaphor is harbour dispatch, interpreted as bold flat handmade paper collage, not a scale model and not an infographic.

A sweeping mustard-yellow waterway enters from the left and branches into three generous curved channels across an ink-dark forest-green paper sea. At the central fork an oversized cut-out black-and-white archival photographic human hand is carefully placing a small lilac paper cargo parcel aboard an appropriately sized lilac workboat. The little workboat takes the central channel. A broad flat barge on one branch carries a long fan of loose paper sheets, while a compact repair tug on the other carries one clearly recognizable black wrench silhouette. Different vessels for different work; the hand's decision and chosen boat are the focal point. The scene should feel witty and observant, not a toy harbor.

Composition: completely flat overhead, sweeping almost calligraphic channels, asymmetrical and confident. All three boats and the selecting hand sit in the broad middle half of the frame, with generous deep green around them. Boats should have unmistakably nautical hull silhouettes. One short cut-paper wake behind the chosen workboat makes its actual path visible. Do not use arrows or explanatory symbols. Make a strong image that reads at 200 pixels, with fewer big shapes rather than tiny details.

Medium: visibly hand-cut colored cardstock and a sharply scissor-cut monochrome photographic hand, sparse screenprinted ink texture, slight paper-edge lift and fine realistic fibers. Treat this as a two-dimensional collage photographed square-on in even diffuse daylight, with tiny interlayer shadows only. Rich deep forest green, confident ochre mustard, subdued lavender/lilac, near-black ink. Mature editorial art, energetic sweeping composition. Full bleed rectangular artwork, no exterior mat, frame, card or UI. No beige or ivory backdrop, no terracotta, no dusty blue. No miniature buildings, gates, slots, trays, folded engineering apparatus, isometric camera, glossy 3D, corporate icon style, ornate maps, text, labels, logos, watermark, charts, measurements, fake code or artificial glow.
alt: A monochrome cut-out hand places a lilac parcel aboard a workboat at a fork in mustard waterways; a barge carries papers and a repair tug carries a wrench along other branches.
cropNotes: The selected hand/parcel/workboat relationship is central and survives a square crop. The two supporting specialist vessels sit toward the right and would be lost or truncated in a centered square, so regenerate a square companion around all three boats if selected. A shallow 2.25:1 crop clips the upper barge and lower repair tug; use the full 16:9 plate or separately recompose that feature size.
review: Accepted as a distinct initial proposal. No accidental text or logos. A strong mustard fork and photographic hand contrast with the rejected ivory tray. The vessels have dimensional folds, but the image overall is a graphic flat collage rather than a miniature apparatus. The parcel transfer makes choice visible; it does not pretend to show measured model performance.
